thread:
Amy (Support): FYI customer @Jim reports model behavior changed after regional failover — responses now missing key sections and tokenization looks off. thread created for escalation  
Jim (ACME): we had a degrade in eu-west-1 ~10:43 UTC so requests were routed to us-east-1. nothing errored, but the summaries are truncated and code blocks are mangled. here's a sample prompt+outputs.  
Jim (ACME): PROMPT: 'Summarize the attached contract highlighting termination clauses.'  
Jim (ACME): Expected: a 4-paragraph human-friendly summary. Actual (after failover): lots of <|unknown|> tokens and odd sentence splits, plus missing legal terms.  
Amy (Support): thanks. do you have one request_id or x-request-id we can use to trace?  
Jim (ACME): request_id=rid-0a1b2c3d, region header eu-west-1, routed_to us-east-1. timestamps below: 2026-02-11T10:43:12Z  
Amy (Support): repro steps I ran (from our side):  
``` 
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'X-Region: eu-west-1' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-infer-v1","input":"Summarize the attached contract..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```  
Amy (Support): on eu-west we got expected output. when I forced region fallback (simulated us-east) I saw the mangled output.  
Matt (eng-oncall): @Zoe can you check routing logs for rid-0a1b2c3d and confirm which model binary was used in us-east? looks like a silent swap to a quantized variant might have happened.  
Zoe (eng-runtime): digging in. routing meta shows fallback_policy=route_to_region, fallback_target=us-east-1, and model_hint_map resolved to redwood-infer-v1-q8 (quantized variant).  
Zoe (eng-runtime): also seeing tokenizer version mismatch: model_metadata[tokenizer_version]=v2.0 while client expected v2.1. That can cause unknown tokens and token split differences.  
Raj (infra): we did activate burst capacity in us-east, those nodes currently run the q8 variant to save memory during overload. looks like the fallback mapping didn't enforce tokenizer parity.  
Terry (product): that's a regression — fallback should not pick variants with different tokenizer configs if request cares about exact text fidelity. we need a short-term mitigation and a longer policy fix.  
Amy (Support): short-term mitigation for customer: 1) pin model version in request (model: "redwood-infer-v1:sha-abcdef") or 2) use routing_policy: region_strict to fail rather than fallback. which can I instruct them?  
Zoe (eng-runtime): both valid. recommending model pin + region_strict for now. also rolling a hotfix to enforce tokenizer compatibility check before accepting fallback.  
Matt (eng-oncall): can we detect and reject silent swaps where tokenizer_version != requested_tokenizer? add a guard in router to prefer failure over mismatched variant.  
Raj (infra): will patch routing table logic to require token_schema match; rolling to staging now.  
Terry (product): assign owners: Zoe -> runtime fix (tokenizer-check), Raj -> routing table change, Amy -> communicate mitigation to customer, Matt -> monitor for other incidents.  
Amy (Support): I've messaged Jim with pin + region_strict steps and asked for confirmation. I also provided the sample request_id and logs.  
Jim (ACME): thanks — implementing pinned model now. will report back if anything else breaks. :thumbsup:  
Zoe (eng-runtime): follow-up: adding telemetry alert when fallback picks quantized variant for requests exceeding a quality threshold; also will emit event when tokenizer_version mismatch is detected.  
deploy-bot: patch rolled to staging (route-tokenizer-guard) at 2026-02-11T11:02:18Z  
Amy (Support): marking this escalated -> eng-runtime and infra. keeping thread open until we confirm customer sees expected outputs with pinning.  
Matt (eng-oncall): thanks everyone. please add any postmortem notes in #postmortems after we confirm fix.
